question: What does it mean for a component to be mounted?
answerGeneral: Mounting is the phase where React creates a component's elements, inserts them into the real DOM for the first time, and runs its setup — componentDidMount in a class, or a useEffect after the first render in a function component. Before mount the component has no DOM presence; after unmount it is removed and its cleanup runs. Mount is the safe point to do things that need the DOM to exist: measuring, focusing, starting subscriptions, fetching.
detailMd:
## What mounting means

Mounting is the moment React first creates a component's elements and inserts them into the real DOM. "Mounted" means the component is live on the page: its DOM nodes exist and you can interact with them.

## The timeline

```
render  ->  MOUNT (DOM created + inserted)  ->  updates…  ->  UNMOUNT (removed)
```

Before mount the component has produced no DOM. After unmount its DOM is gone and its cleanup has run.

## Why the mount point matters

Some work can only happen once the DOM exists — measuring an element, focusing an input, attaching a third-party widget, starting a subscription, fetching initial data. Mount is the safe moment for all of it:

```jsx
useEffect(() => {
  inputRef.current.focus(); // node exists now
}, []); // [] -> runs once, right after mount
```

In a class component this is `componentDidMount`.

## Mount and unmount pair up

Anything you start on mount you should stop on unmount — timers, listeners, sockets — or it leaks. `useEffect`'s cleanup return is built for exactly this symmetry:

```jsx
useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(tick, 1000);
  return () => clearInterval(id); // runs on unmount
}, []);
```
answerGeneralTr: Mounting, React'in bir component'in elemanlarını oluşturduğu, onları ilk kez gerçek DOM'a eklediği ve kurulumunu çalıştırdığı evredir — bir class'ta componentDidMount ya da bir function component'te ilk render'dan sonraki bir useEffect. Mount'tan önce component'in DOM varlığı yoktur; unmount'tan sonra kaldırılır ve cleanup'ı çalışır. Mount, DOM'un var olmasını gerektiren şeyleri yapmak için güvenli noktadır: ölçmek, focus vermek, abonelik başlatmak, veri çekmek.

question: What is Flow?
answerGeneral: Flow is a static type checker for JavaScript built by Facebook, from the same era React came from. You add type annotations and Flow catches type errors — including null and undefined misuse — without changing how the code runs. It solves the same problem as TypeScript, and historically some React codebases used it. TypeScript has since won the ecosystem decisively, so new React projects use TypeScript; Flow is mostly something you meet in older Facebook-origin code.
detailMd:
## What Flow is

Flow is a static type checker for JavaScript, created by Facebook around the same time React rose. You annotate code with types, and Flow checks them without changing how the code runs — annotations are stripped at build time.

```js
// @flow
function greet(name: string): string {
  return `Hi ${name}`;
}
```

## What it gives you

The usual benefits of static typing: catching type mismatches before runtime, flagging `null` and `undefined` misuse, and better editor autocomplete. Conceptually it solves the same problem as TypeScript.

## Flow vs TypeScript

For a few years they were genuine alternatives, and several large React codebases used Flow. Over time TypeScript won the ecosystem decisively: better tooling, far wider library type coverage through DefinitelyTyped, and broader adoption.

## What this means today

New React projects use TypeScript — it is effectively the default, and this project is no exception. Flow is now something you mostly meet in older Facebook-origin codebases. Worth recognising in an interview, but not what you would choose for a new project.
answerGeneralTr: Flow, Facebook tarafından, React'in çıktığı dönemde yapılmış, JavaScript için statik bir tip kontrolcüsüdür. Tip anotasyonları eklersin ve Flow, kodun nasıl çalıştığını değiştirmeden tip hatalarını — null ve undefined yanlış kullanımı dahil — yakalar. TypeScript ile aynı problemi çözer ve tarihsel olarak bazı React kod tabanları onu kullandı. O zamandan beri TypeScript ekosistemi kesin biçimde kazandı, yani yeni React projeleri TypeScript kullanır; Flow çoğunlukla eski, Facebook kökenli kodda karşılaşacağın bir şeydir.

question: What is the point of shouldComponentUpdate()?
answerGeneral: shouldComponentUpdate is a class-component lifecycle method that returns a boolean to tell React whether a re-render is worth doing. Returning false skips rendering that component and its subtree — a performance optimisation when you know the output cannot have changed. PureComponent implements it automatically with a shallow prop and state comparison. The function-component equivalent is wrapping the component in React.memo, which does the same shallow check on props.
answerGeneralTr: shouldComponentUpdate, React'e bir yeniden render'ın yapmaya değer olup olmadığını söyleyen, bir boolean döndüren bir class-component lifecycle metodudur. false döndürmek o component'i ve alt ağacını render etmeyi atlar — çıktının değişmiş olamayacağını bildiğinde bir performans optimizasyonu. PureComponent onu sığ bir prop ve state karşılaştırmasıyla otomatik uygular. Function-component karşılığı, component'i React.memo ile sarmaktır; o da prop'larda aynı sığ kontrolü yapar.

question: What are PropTypes in React?
answerGeneral: PropTypes is a runtime type-checking mechanism for component props. You declare the expected shape — Component.propTypes = { count: PropTypes.number.isRequired } — and in development React warns in the console when a prop is missing or the wrong type. It was the standard before TypeScript adoption. Today TypeScript covers the same need at compile time, more thoroughly, so new code uses TS prop types instead and PropTypes mostly lingers in older codebases.
answerGeneralTr: PropTypes, component prop'ları için bir runtime tip kontrol mekanizmasıdır. Beklenen şekli bildirirsin — Component.propTypes = { count: PropTypes.number.isRequired } — ve development'ta bir prop eksik ya da yanlış tipte olduğunda React konsolda uyarır. TypeScript benimsenmeden önce standarttı. Bugün TypeScript aynı ihtiyacı derleme zamanında, daha kapsamlı karşılıyor, yani yeni kod onun yerine TS prop tipleri kullanır ve PropTypes çoğunlukla eski kod tabanlarında kalır.

question: What is the difference between useRef and createRef?
answerGeneral: Both produce a ref object with a .current property, but their lifetime differs. createRef makes a fresh ref every time it runs — correct in a class component where it runs once in the constructor, but wrong in a function component, where it would be recreated on every render. useRef creates the ref once and returns the same object across all renders of that component. So in function components you always use useRef; createRef is the class-component tool.
detailMd:
## Both make a ref object

`useRef` and `createRef` both return an object with a `.current` property that you attach via the `ref` attribute. The difference is lifetime.

## createRef — a fresh ref each call

`createRef()` creates a brand-new ref object every time it runs. That is correct in a class component, where it runs once in the constructor:

```jsx
class Form extends React.Component {
  inputRef = React.createRef(); // created once
}
```

## useRef — a stable ref across renders

`useRef()` creates the ref on the first render and returns the same object on every render after. In a function component this is what you need — `createRef` there would make a new ref every render and lose `.current`:

```jsx
function Form() {
  const inputRef = useRef(null); // same object every render
  return <input ref={inputRef} />;
}
```

## The rule

In function components, always `useRef`. `createRef` is the class-component tool. They are not interchangeable — using `createRef` in a function component is a real bug.

## One more useRef power

`useRef` is not only for DOM nodes. Because writing `.current` does not trigger a re-render, it is also the place to hold any mutable value that should persist across renders — a timer id, a previous value — without causing one.
answerGeneralTr: İkisi de .current property'sine sahip bir ref object'i üretir, ama ömürleri farklıdır. createRef her çalıştığında taze bir ref yapar — constructor'da bir kez çalıştığı bir class component'te doğru, ama her render'da yeniden oluşturulacağı bir function component'te yanlış. useRef ise ref'i bir kez oluşturur ve o component'in tüm render'ları boyunca aynı object'i döndürür. Yani function component'lerde her zaman useRef kullanırsın; createRef class-component aracıdır.

question: What are Pure Components?
answerGeneral: A PureComponent is a class component that implements shouldComponentUpdate with a shallow comparison of props and state — it skips re-rendering when neither changed by reference. It saves wasted renders for components with stable inputs. The catch is the comparison is shallow, so a mutated object or a new inline object or function passed as a prop defeats it. The function-component equivalent is React.memo, with the same shallow-compare behaviour and the same caveat.
detailMd:
## What a PureComponent is `React.PureComponent` is a class component that automatically implements `shouldComponentUpdate` with a shallow comparison of props and state. It re-renders only when one of them actually changed by reference. ```jsx class Row extends React.PureComponent { render() { return
  • {this.props.item.label}
    • ; } } ``` A regular `Component` re-renders whenever its parent does; a `PureComponent` skips the render when its inputs look unchanged. ## The shallow-comparison catch "Shallow" means it compares each prop and state value by reference, one level deep. Two consequences: - **Mutation is invisible.** Mutate an object instead of replacing it and the reference is unchanged, so the PureComponent skips a render it should have done. - **New references defeat it.** An inline object, array, or arrow function — `style={{}}`, `onClick={() => …}` — is a new reference every render, so the comparison always sees a change. ## The function-component equivalent `React.memo` does the same shallow-prop check for function components. Pair it with `useMemo` and `useCallback` to keep prop references stable so the memo actually holds. ## Use with judgement It is an optimisation, and the comparison itself costs something. Apply it to components that re-render often with genuinely stable props — not everywhere by default.
answerGeneralTr: PureComponent, shouldComponentUpdate'i prop'ların ve state'in sığ bir karşılaştırmasıyla uygulayan bir class component'tir — ikisi de referans olarak değişmediğinde yeniden render'ı atlar. Stabil girdileri olan component'ler için boşa render'ları önler. İşin püf noktası, karşılaştırmanın sığ olmasıdır; yani değiştirilen bir object ya da prop olarak geçilen yeni bir inline object veya fonksiyon onu boşa çıkarır. Function-component karşılığı React.memo'dur; aynı sığ-karşılaştırma davranışı ve aynı uyarıyla.
